scope: Companion to source-content.json: public evidence links for the approved 04 page. Includes the approved WHO example, COVIED wording, and Carter decision-tools link. The original 04 embedded content packet is synchronized; other historical gallery variants are not regenerated.

links.label: WHO’s toolkit on reaching people missed by treatment campaigns
links.evidence: Published WHO/PAHO toolkit names Lee in its core drafting group (PDF pages 10 and 113) and cites his input in the communication section (PDF page 62). Existing primary career records support his communication-guidance contribution; this is not sole authorship of the toolkit.

links.label: Decision tools
links.evidence: PDF page 24 / printed page 21 reports Lee's March 2023 presentation on supply-planning prototypes and an organizational-learning blueprint. Link supports practical program-design work, not a claim of nationwide deployment or measured campaign impact.

links.label: COVID-19 vaccination campaigns
links.evidence: Slide 34 places Emory/HELP ethnographic research, focus groups, and interviews in COVIED message development. Lee's project role is corroborated by his career record; the link does not attribute the whole coalition toolkit to Lee.

links.label: learning from campaign delivery
links.evidence: 2020 PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases Port-au-Prince case study names Lee T. Wilkers as coauthor, credited for formal analysis and review/editing. It examines stakeholder experience and organizational learning in declining LF-MDA coverage. Link belongs under program design and organizational learning; Lee requested removing the IPV project from community engagement.

links.label: evaluation frameworks
links.evidence: PDF page 19, footnote 13 cites the HELP-UNICEF knowledge-architecture report. Local fact base identifies Lee as a report author. Does not claim authorship of the coalition's whole strategy.

links.label: gaps between hospital care and community support
links.evidence: 2024 article names Lee Wilkers as coauthor. Link attaches to the hospital/community-care finding, not to the separate survivor-interview methods.

links.label: Brokered Dialogue
links.evidence: MESA identifies the Emory-produced gene-drive dialogue and provides a VIEW link to the film. Local fact base corroborates Lee's production/analysis role.

links.label: Compassion in global health
links.evidence: Official FACE account of the March 2026 Epidemiology of Compassion special issue. Local record supports Lee's planning and operational contributions, not article authorship or guest editorship. Keep this a linked label only.

links.label: Focus Area for Compassion and Ethics (FACE)
Evans Research Group
links.evidence: Official Emory profile for Dabney Evans, with relevant IPV and app research. No dedicated Emory group page was found. Do not use evansresearchgroup.org: that is an unrelated polymer-chemistry lab.

links.label: Center for Humanitarian Emergencies
links.evidence: Official center page. Existing 2023-2024 historical role stays unchanged; current certificate availability does not change Lee's past work.

links.label: Human Engagement Learning Platform (HELP)
links.evidence: Official Emory explanation of HELP and stakeholder engagement, using the verified redirect destination. It predates Lee's appointment and is used for program context, not personal attribution. Former helpforglobalhealth.com was not verifiable.

links.label: Franklin Microbial Ecology Lab
links.evidence: Lab's own people page explicitly lists Lee Wilkers as an undergraduate researcher, Fall 2013-Summer 2014. Graduate history is separately supported by the local fact base and Franklin CV.
